access_links.label: Port of Rotterdam flood risk management

dedupe_keys.name: port of rotterdam flood adaptation strategy for the port outside the dikes 2021 2022

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the adaptation strategy that the Port of Rotterdam Authority developed with the municipality, other government bodies and port companies for Europe's largest port, which handled over 460 million tonnes in 2022 on 4,600 hectares outside the Dutch dike system. Using sea level projections from the Rijkswaterstaat Hydra-NL database with KNMI scenarios (a range of 26 to 124 cm by 2100), it works with 35 cm by 2050 and 85 cm by 2100. Flood risks were modelled per port area and sorted by companies and public authorities into acceptable and not acceptable, and measures were chosen per area: prevention (raising quays and slopes, compartments), spatial adaptation, and crisis management, each assigned to a time horizon from immediate to after 2100. The cost-benefit analysis gives present-value costs of almost EUR 90 million against EUR 611 million of avoided damage, a ratio of 6.8. The strategy was notified to port companies in September 2022 and will be reviewed about every ten years. The page was published in March 2025 and is accessible online as free HTML with links to the port's water safety pages and the Dutch strategy report. Caveats: the flood models and area results are in the port's documents, not on the page, and implementation depends on private operators. The case illustrates flood hazard exposure, investment appraisal and climate adaptation for a seaport; related records are the World Port Index and IMF PortWatch.
name: Port of Rotterdam flood adaptation strategy for the port outside the dikes (2021-2022)
outcomes: A per-area package of prevention, spatial and crisis measures was adopted with present-value costs of almost EUR 90 million against EUR 611 million of avoided flood damage (benefit-cost ratio 6.8).
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on the Port of Rotterdam Authority
